#### Proposed Changes ####

`prePullImages` reads the pre-pull image list with a `bufio.Scanner` and never checks `scanner.Err()`. This adds the check, appending any read error to the `errs` slice the function already returns.

`Scan()` returns `false` for a clean end of input and for a failed read, and the two cannot be told apart from the loop alone. Since `errors.Join` of an empty slice is `nil`, a list that could not be read comes back as `([], nil)`: a success that pulled nothing.

Two reachable triggers, both on the drop-in images directory:

* A line longer than `bufio.MaxScanTokenSize` (64KiB) gives `bufio.ErrTooLong`. A binary file or a tarball accidentally named `.txt` and dropped in the images directory hits that on its first line, so nothing is pre-pulled and nothing says so.
* An I/O error partway through leaves the images before the error pulled and the rest not, which is the worse case because it looks like it worked.

In both cases `preloadFile` sees `err == nil`, logs `Pulling images from <path>`, and carries on. On an air-gapped node the operator finds out later from `ImagePullBackOff` on pods, with no log line pointing at the list that was never fully read.

With the check, the wrap already in `preloadFile` produces:

```
failed to pull images from /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images/images.txt: bufio.Scanner: token too long
```

I only changed this one site. There are two other unchecked `bufio.Scanner` loops, both in `pkg/cgroups/cgroups_linux.go`, reading `/proc/self/cgroup` and `/proc/1/cgroup`. Those lines are short and I could not demonstrate a reachable read failure on procfs, so adding the check there would be defensive noise and I left them alone.

The pattern is already in the tree: `pkg/agent/config/config.go:398`, `pkg/dataverify/dataverify.go:103` and `pkg/agent/templates/templates.go:410` all check `scanner.Err()`, and this file uses `errors.Join(errs...)` in five places to report partial failure.

#### Types of Changes ####

Bugfix. Six lines in `pkg/agent/containerd/containerd.go` plus a unit test.

#### Verification ####

```
gofmt -l pkg/agent/containerd/                 # no output
GOOS=linux go build ./pkg/agent/containerd/    # ok
GOOS=linux go vet ./pkg/agent/containerd/      # ok
go test ./pkg/agent/containerd/                # 0 failures
```

The package does not build on darwin, since `socketPrefix` and `templateFuncs` are only defined in the `_linux` and `_windows` files, so the tests were cross-compiled for linux and run in a linux container rather than on my host.

#### Testing ####

Yes, `Test_UnitPrePullImages` in `pkg/agent/containerd/prepull_test.go`. It needs no mocks: in all four cases the loop body never parses an image name, so the image service and the CRI client are never reached and can be left unconfigured.

Reverting the six-line change and rerunning it gives:

```
--- PASS: Test_UnitPrePullImages/empty_list
--- PASS: Test_UnitPrePullImages/blank_lines_only
--- FAIL: Test_UnitPrePullImages/read_fails        (images=0 err=<nil>)
--- FAIL: Test_UnitPrePullImages/line_too_long     (images=0 err=<nil>)
```

The two clean inputs keep passing without the change, which is the half I cared about: the new check does not report an error where there is none. The two error inputs fail without it, so they are not testing nothing.

Happy to drop the test if you would rather keep this to the six-line change, or to widen it if you want the cgroups sites covered too.

#### Linked Issues ####

None. CONTRIBUTING.md says a small fix can go straight to a PR, so I did not open an issue first. Glad to file one if you would prefer it tracked.

#### User-Facing Change ####

```release-note
Errors encountered while reading a pre-pull image list are now reported instead of being treated as the end of the list.
```

#### Further Comments ####

I found this with a small AST pass over the tree looking for `for scanner.Scan()` loops that never call `Err()` on the scanner, resolving each receiver back to its `bufio.NewScanner` call so that the many `rows.Scan(...)` call sites are not caught up in it. No linter in the current set reports this shape: `errcheck` cannot see it because `Scan()` returns a `bool` rather than an error, and `staticcheck` has no check for it. Of the seven scanner loops in the tree, four already check `Err()`, and of the three that do not, this is the one where the input is a user-supplied file rather than procfs.
